figures.caption: Figure 1: Examples of highly efficient codes. a. The eigenvalues λn = π2 T 2n 2 of Fourier filters as a function of n. b. The first five Fourier filters are low order sinusoids. c. Result of Bayesoptimal decoding of a signal f(t) (black) from neural activity r (see Eq. 16) assuming Fourier filters and N = 5 or N = 10 neurons. Note that the population essentially provides a Fourier series reconstruction of the signal. d. The first five Legendre polynomial filters. Like the Fourier filters, higher-order eigenfunctions have more temporal variation.
